subject: Science
question: Objects that emit or give out light of their own (such as the Sun, stars, a lit candle, an electric torch) are called:
explanation: Luminous objects radiate their own photon emissions directly (e.g. the Sun, electric bulb, candle flame).

subject: Science
question: Objects that do NOT emit light of their own and become visible only when light falls on them (such as the Moon, a chair, a book) are called:
explanation: Non-luminous bodies (including the Moon, which reflects sunlight) do not generate intrinsic light.

subject: Science
question: Materials that allow light to pass through them completely and clearly, so that objects behind them can be seen distinctly (such as clear glass, air, clean water) are called:
explanation: Transparent media transmit light rays with negligible absorption and scattering, permitting sharp visual transmission.

subject: Science
question: Materials that do NOT allow ANY light to pass through them at all, so that we cannot see through them (such as a wooden board, brick wall, metal plate) are called:
explanation: Opaque materials completely absorb and reflect incident light, blocking optical transmission.

subject: Science
question: Materials that allow light to pass through them only partially, so that objects behind them can be seen only faintly or hazily (such as butter paper, frosted glass, oily paper) are called:
explanation: Translucent media transmit light diffusely, scattering photons so images behind appear indistinct.

subject: Science
question: A dark patch formed on a surface behind an opaque object when it blocks the straight path of light is called a:
explanation: A shadow is an umbral region of darkness cast when an opaque body obstructs rectilinear light propagation.

subject: Science
question: What three essential things are required to form and view a Shadow?
options: A Source of Light, an Opaque Object, and a Screen (surface)
A Mirror, a Candle, and Water
explanation: Shadow formation strictly necessitates 1. an incident light source, 2. an obstructing opaque object, and 3. a screen/surface to cast upon.

subject: Science
question: The fundamental scientific principle that light travels strictly in STRAIGHT LINES is known as:
explanation: Rectilinear propagation states that optical rays travel along straight linear trajectories in a homogeneous medium.

subject: Science
question: What simple optical device consisting of a box with a tiny pinhole aperture at one end produces an INVERTED (upside-down) image on a translucent screen without using any glass lens?
explanation: A pinhole camera exploits rectilinear light paths crossing through a minute aperture to project an inverted real image.

subject: Science
question: The bouncing back of light rays when they strike a smooth, polished, highly reflective surface (such as a plane mirror or still water surface) is called:
explanation: Reflection is the redirection of incident light waves at an interface according to the laws of reflection.

subject: Science
question: What are the characteristics of the image of our face formed in a standard Plane Mirror?
options: Erect (upright), same size as the object, laterally inverted (left appears right), and formed at the same distance behind the mirror
explanation: A plane mirror forms a virtual, erect, equi-distant, unmagnified, laterally inverted image.

subject: Science
question: What natural pinhole images can be observed on the ground under a dense tree during bright daylight?
options: Circular bright patches of light (which are actually pinhole images of the Sun formed by tiny gaps between overlapping leaves)
explanation: Gaps between leafy canopies act as natural pinhole apertures, projecting circular solar images onto the ground.

subject: Science
question: What is the crucial difference between a 'Shadow' and an 'Image' formed by a mirror?
options: A Shadow is only a dark outline showing the shape of an object without any color or details; an Image shows the full color, facial details, and features of the object formed by reflected light
A Shadow is colorful while an image is black
A Shadow is formed by mirrors
explanation: Shadows represent absence of light displaying silhouette geometry; optical images reproduce chromatic wavelengths and surface textures.

subject: Science
question: Why can we NOT see the flame of a lit candle when looking through a BENT or curved plastic pipe, whereas we can see it clearly through a STRAIGHT pipe?
options: Because light travels only in straight lines (Rectilinear propagation) and cannot bend around the corners of a curved pipe
Because the bent pipe blows out the candle flame
Because candle light is too heavy to travel up a pipe
Because curved pipes absorb all oxygen
explanation: Light cannot spontaneously negotiate curvature without reflective mirrors, proving straight-line rectilinear transmission.

subject: Science
question: Why does the color of a shadow NOT change when a red ball, a green book, or a yellow toy blocks white light?
options: Because a shadow is merely an area of darkness where light was completely blocked from reaching the screen, regardless of the object's surface color
Because all shadows are painted black by nature
Because colored light is absorbed by the ground
Because human eyes only see black
explanation: Shadows are regions of photon deprivation (umbra); chromatic properties of the blocking opaque object do not affect the darkness.

subject: Science
question: What is 'Lateral Inversion' observed when you raise your left hand in front of a plane mirror?
options: The phenomenon where the left side of the object appears as the right side in the mirror image, and the right side appears as the left side
explanation: Front-to-back ray reflection reverses apparent lateral chirality: left hand maps to the image's right hand.

subject: Science
question: Why is the word 'AMBULANCE' printed backwards ('ECNALUBMA') on the front of emergency hospital vans?
options: So that drivers looking into their rear-view mirrors see the laterally inverted reflection read forward and correctly as 'AMBULANCE'
Because of a printing machine mistake
To make the van look foreign
explanation: Pre-inverting the lettering ensures that lateral inversion in planar rear-view mirrors restores legible front-facing orthography.

subject: Science
question: What happens to the size of a shadow when an opaque object is moved CLOSER to the light source (with the screen position fixed)?
options: The size of the shadow INCREASES (becomes larger)
The size of the shadow decreases
The shadow turns into an image
explanation: Moving closer intercepts a broader angular divergence cone of light rays, casting a larger geometric shadow cone on the screen.

subject: Science
question: Why does a high-flying aeroplane or a bird soaring very high in the clear sky NOT cast a visible shadow on the ground?
options: Because at great altitudes, the dark central shadow (umbra) tapers off in air and only faint penumbra reaches the ground, making the shadow imperceptible
Because birds are transparent to sunlight
Because aeroplanes fly faster than light
explanation: Due to the finite angular size of the Sun, the umbral cone terminates before reaching ground level, dispersing ambient light.

subject: Science
question: How does the image formed in a Pinhole Camera change if the tiny pinhole is replaced by a LARGE open hole (e.g. 2 cm diameter)?
options: The image becomes completely blurred and unclear because multiple overlapping images enter through different points of the large hole
The image becomes super sharp and magnified
The image turns black and white
explanation: A large aperture acts as infinite adjacent pinholes, creating overlapping circles of confusion that blur optical fidelity.

subject: Science
question: Why is an image formed in a pinhole camera always INVERTED (upside down)?
options: Light rays from the top of the object travel in a straight line through the pinhole to strike the bottom of the screen, while rays from the bottom strike the top
Because the camera box is upside down
Because air rotates light rays by 180°
explanation: Intersecting rectilinear ray trajectories cross linearly at the focal aperture, projecting top points to bottom screen coordinates.

subject: Science
question: Why is the Moon classified as a NON-LUMINOUS object, despite shining brilliantly in the night sky?
options: The Moon does not produce any light through nuclear fusion or heat; it merely reflects incident sunlight striking its rocky dusty surface
Because it is covered with ice
Because it only shines for a few hours
Because it is too far from Earth
explanation: Lunar regolith has an albedo of ~0.12, reflecting solar irradiation without generating autonomous luminescent energy.

subject: Science
question: What optical device uses two parallel plane mirrors fixed at 45° angles inside a Z-shaped tube to allow a person to see over walls or around corners (used in submarines to view surface ships)?
explanation: A periscope utilizes twin 45° plane mirrors to reflect incoming horizontal rays downward and then horizontally into the observer's eye.

subject: Science
question: What biological organism is a natural living LUMINOUS animal that emits glowing yellow-green light through bioluminescence in the dark?
explanation: Fireflies exhibit enzymatic bioluminescence (luciferin oxidized by luciferase in the presence of ATP) to emit cold light.

subject: Science
question: Can a transparent glass sheet cast a dark, distinct shadow on the wall?
options: No, because transparent glass allows almost all light rays to pass directly through without obstruction
Yes, exactly like a thick wooden door
Yes, if the light is turned off
Yes, if the glass is round
explanation: High optical transmittance prevents significant light blockage, resulting in no discernible umbral shadow.

subject: Science
question: How do the shadows of objects cast by the Sun change in length during the course of a clear sunny day?
options: Shadows are longest in the early morning and late evening (when Sun is low on horizon), and shortest at solar noon (when Sun is highest overhead)
Shadow length remains exactly constant all day
explanation: Shadow length L = h / tan(θ), where θ is solar elevation angle; low morning/evening solar altitudes yield elongated shadows.

subject: Science
question: Why can we NOT see anything when entering a pitch-dark room without any light source?
options: Our eyes do not emit light; vision requires light from a luminous source to reflect off objects and enter our eyes
Because dark rooms make human eyes close automatically
Because darkness turns objects invisible permanently
Because light rays freeze in dark rooms
explanation: Photoreceptors in the retina require incoming reflected photons to trigger neuro-electrical optic nerve impulses.

subject: Science
question: What is an Eclipse (Solar or Lunar) in astronomical science?
options: A colossal natural shadow phenomenon formed in space when an astronomical body (Moon or Earth) blocks sunlight from reaching another body
A magical storm on the Sun
The Sun turning off for a few minutes
explanation: Eclipses are large-scale celestial shadow events governed by rectilinear light propagation across astronomical orbits.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A).
explanation: Pinhole projection eliminates high-intensity infrared and ultraviolet macular burns by redirecting diffuse illumination to a projection screen.

explanation: 'Clear optical window glass' is TRANSPARENT (not translucent) because it transmits light clearly without diffuse scattering.

subject: Science
question: A student holds a circular disc between a point source of light and a white screen. How can the circular disc cast an OVAL or ELLIPTICAL shadow on the screen?
options: By tilting the disc at an angle (oblique orientation) relative to the incident light beam
By moving the screen further away
A circular disc can never cast an elliptical shadow
explanation: Projective geometry: the cross-sectional silhouette of an inclined circle projected along rectilinear rays onto a planar screen forms an ellipse.

explanation: Luminous = emits light; Translucent = partial transmission; Rectilinear = straight lines; Reflection = bouncing.

subject: Science
question: What is the physical nature of the two regions of a shadow cast by an extended light source (like a large frosted bulb)?
options: Umbra (the central completely dark region receiving zero light) and Penumbra (the outer partially illuminated grey region receiving partial light)
explanation: An extended source generates a total geometric shadow cone (umbra) flanked by an annular partial shadow cone (penumbra).

question: If you stand 2 metres in front of a flat plane mirror, what is the total distance between YOU and your virtual IMAGE in the mirror?
options: 4 metres (2 m in front + 2 m behind the mirror)
explanation: Object distance = Image distance (d_o = d_i = 2 m). Total separation between object and image = 2 + 2 = 4 metres.

subject: Science
question: Why does a rough unpolished surface (like a chalk wall or unpolished wood) NOT form a clear mirror image, despite reflecting light into our eyes?
options: Microscopic surface irregularities cause Diffuse (Irregular) Reflection, scattering reflected light rays in all random directions rather than parallel reflection
Because chalk absorbs all light completely
explanation: Specular reflection from planar mirrors maintains parallel wavefronts; microscopic rugosity produces diffuse multi-directional scattering.

subject: Science
question: An experimenter constructs a pinhole camera with an adjustable sliding box. What happens to the projected image on the screen when the screen is moved FURTHER away from the pinhole?

The image becomes smaller and brighter
explanation: Linear divergence magnifies image height h_i = h_o · (v/u), while photon flux spreads over a greater surface area, reducing luminous illuminance.

subject: Science
question: What is the speed of light in vacuum (c), representing the absolute cosmic speed limit in physics?

subject: Science
question: Why is an image formed in a plane mirror called a 'VIRTUAL Image' in physics?
options: Because reflected light rays only appear to diverge from a point behind the mirror and cannot be captured or focused on a physical screen placed there
Because it exists only in computer software
Because it is fake and painted
Because it disappears when we blink
explanation: Virtual images are formed by the imaginary backwards extrapolation of diverging reflected rays and cannot be projected on a real screen.

To go on a world tour

To take 50 pills a day in a dark room
To stay in bed without food
To move to the cold mountains
explanation: The doctor prescribed normal diet plus one hour of daily morning sunshine and fresh air as essential medicine.

subject: English
question: To whom did little Saeeda make a heartfelt secret pact/prayer in the courtyard in the evening?

explanation: Saeeda made a solemn pact with the evening sunrays to arrive the following morning with warmth for her mother.

Uncle scolded and beat him harshly
explanation: Uncle consoled Rasheed with gifts and explained how the shopkeeper tricked naive customers.

They were the luckiest people in the world

subject: English

Rasheed was born under an unlucky star

subject: English
question: What happened when the bright, warm morning sunrays bathed Saeeda's mother as she lay in the courtyard?

question: Why was the shopkeeper described as 'neither too young nor too old, neither smart nor lazy'?

Because he was a king in disguise

As a golden clock in the sky

The absolute superiority of city life over village life

chapter: Chapter 8: Environmental Studies, Biodiversity & Wildlife Conservation of India

chapter: Chapter 8: Environmental Studies, Biodiversity & Wildlife Conservation of India

chapter: Chapter 8: Environmental Studies, Biodiversity & Wildlife Conservation of India

chapter: Chapter 8: Environmental Studies, Biodiversity & Wildlife Conservation of India

A city with many zoo parks

The magnification of cells under a microscope

chapter: Chapter 8: India — Climate, Vegetation and Wildlife

subject: Social Science

chapter: Chapter 8: India — Climate, Vegetation and Wildlife

Because snow melts in the Himalayas
Because the Arabian sea dries up
Because clouds move only in circles

subject: Social Science
chapter: Chapter 8: India — Climate, Vegetation and Wildlife

Number of cars, houses, trains, and planes
Types of soil, rocks, metals, and minerals
Color of clouds, birds, rivers, and trees

subject: Social Science
chapter: Chapter 8: India — Climate, Vegetation and Wildlife

Because coastal cities have more air conditioners
Because the sun doesn't shine on oceans

subject: Social Science
chapter: Chapter 8: India — Climate, Vegetation and Wildlife

subject: Social Science
chapter: Chapter 8: India — Climate, Vegetation and Wildlife

subject: Social Science
chapter: Chapter 8: India — Climate, Vegetation and Wildlife

subject: Social Science
chapter: Chapter 8: India — Climate, Vegetation and Wildlife

Forests that grow on mountaintops in snow

subject: Social Science
chapter: Chapter 8: India — Climate, Vegetation and Wildlife

subject: Social Science
chapter: Chapter 8: India — Climate, Vegetation and Wildlife

subject: Social Science
chapter: Chapter 8: India — Climate, Vegetation and Wildlife

subject: Social Science

In the Thar Desert of Rajasthan
In the cold deserts of Ladakh

subject: Social Science
chapter: Chapter 8: India — Climate, Vegetation and Wildlife

options: Wild Yaks, Tibetan Antelope (Chiru), Snow Leopards, and Himalayan Ibex
explanation: High alpine Himalayan fauna features thick pelts: Bos mutus (Wild Yak), Chiru, Snow Leopards, and Bharal (Blue Sheep).

subject: Social Science
chapter: Chapter 8: India — Climate, Vegetation and Wildlife
question: What are 'Migratory Birds' and why do birds like Siberian Cranes, Flamingos, and Pintail Ducks migrate to Indian wetlands every winter?
options: They fly thousands of kilometres from freezing Arctic/Siberian winter extremes to warmer Indian wetlands in search of food and nesting grounds
They migrate because they get lost
They come to India to hibernate underwater
explanation: Migratory avifauna escape freezing sub-polar temperatures along the Central Asian Flyway to winter in hospitable Indian wetlands.

subject: Social Science
chapter: Chapter 8: India — Climate, Vegetation and Wildlife
question: Which desert animals are specially adapted to the arid Rann of Kachchh and Thar Desert of northwestern India?
options: Camels (in Thar) and Wild Ass / Khur (in the Little Rann of Kachchh)
explanation: The Indian Wild Ass (Equus hemionus khur) thrives in the saline flats of Rann of Kachchh alongside desert camels.

subject: Social Science
chapter: Chapter 8: India — Climate, Vegetation and Wildlife
question: What civic programme was launched to encourage people and school students across India to plant millions of trees during the monsoon season?
explanation: Initiated by K.M. Munshi in 1950, Van Mahotsav is an annual tree-planting festival celebrated in the first week of July.

subject: Social Science
chapter: Chapter 8: India — Climate, Vegetation and Wildlife
question: Why is agriculture in India predominantly described as a 'Gamble with the Monsoons'?
options: A vast majority of Indian farming relies on timely, adequate monsoon rainfall; a weak or delayed monsoon causes severe drought and crop failure
Because farmers play card games in fields
explanation: Rainfed agrarian livelihoods depend heavily on the spatio-temporal distribution of southwest monsoonal rains.

subject: Social Science
chapter: Chapter 8: India — Climate, Vegetation and Wildlife
question:
Read the statements:
Assertion (A): Tropical Rainforests exhibit a complex, multi-layered vertical canopy structure where little sunlight reaches the ground floor.
Reason (R): High equatorial temperature, torrential year-round rainfall, and fertile humus foster intense biological competition, driving trees to soar up to 60 metres in height.
Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A).
explanation: Canopy stratification (emergent, upper canopy, understory, forest floor) maximizes photosynthetic solar capture in dense rainforests.

subject: Social Science
chapter: Chapter 8: India — Climate, Vegetation and Wildlife
question:
Spot the IMPOSTER in the following group of trees classified by their natural forest type:
Group: [Ebony (Evergreen), Mahogany (Evergreen), Rosewood (Evergreen), Teak (Evergreen)]
explanation: Teak (Tectona grandis) is a classic TROPICAL DECIDUOUS tree, NOT an evergreen rainforest tree.

subject: Social Science
chapter: Chapter 8: India — Climate, Vegetation and Wildlife
question: A climatologist records the seasonal pressure patterns over South Asia in July. What atmospheric mechanism drives the Southwest Monsoon?
options: Intense solar heating creates an intense thermal Low-Pressure trough over the northwestern plains/Tibetan plateau, sucking in moist High-Pressure oceanic trade winds from the southern Indian Ocean
Cold snow in the Himalayas blows wind to the sea
The moon pulls all ocean water onto the land
Earth stops rotating for a month
explanation: Thermal depression over the continental interior draws cross-equatorial Coriolis-deflected southwesterly trade winds carrying ocean moisture.

subject: Social Science
chapter: Chapter 8: India — Climate, Vegetation and Wildlife
question:
Match Column I (Forest Types) with Column II (Dominant Species / Typical Regions):
(a) Tropical Rainforest  -> (i) Sundari / Ganga-Brahmaputra delta
(b) Tropical Deciduous   -> (ii) Ebony, Mahogany, Rosewood / Western Ghats
(c) Coniferous Mountain   -> (iii) Sal, Teak, Peepal, Shisham / Central India
(d) Mangrove Forest      -> (iv) Chir, Pine, Deodar / Himalayan slopes
explanation: Rainforest = Ebony/Mahogany; Deciduous = Sal/Teak; Coniferous = Chir/Deodar; Mangrove = Sundari.

subject: Social Science
chapter: Chapter 8: India — Climate, Vegetation and Wildlife
question:
Read the statements regarding Indian climate and forests:
Statement 1: Western slopes of the Western Ghats receive over 250 cm of orographic rainfall and support Tropical Evergreen rainforests.
Statement 2: The eastern leeward side of the Western Ghats lies in the rain-shadow zone and receives significantly lower rainfall.
Statement 3: Coniferous trees shed all their leaves in summer.
Which statements are TRUE?
explanation: Statement 3 is false because coniferous gymnosperms are evergreen and retain needle foliage through winter. Statements 1 and 2 are true.

subject: Social Science
chapter: Chapter 8: India — Climate, Vegetation and Wildlife
question: Why do plants in thorny scrub forests (like Acacia/Babool, Cactus, and Khejri) develop extensive underground root networks stretching meters deep and wide?
options: To maximize groundwater scavenging across deep arid soil profiles where surface moisture is scarce
explanation: Deep phreatophytic taproots reach capillary fringe water tables, sustaining desert scrub in xerophytic environments.

subject: Social Science
chapter: Chapter 8: India — Climate, Vegetation and Wildlife
question:
Consider four national conservation sanctuaries:
1. Gir National Park
2. Kaziranga National Park
3. Dachigam National Park
4. Keibul Lamjao National Park
Match the exclusive endemic flagship species protected in each in order (1, 2, 3, 4):
options: 1: Asiatic Lion ; 2: One-Horned Rhino ; 3: Hangul (Kashmir Stag) ; 4: Sangai (Dancing Deer)
1: Snow Leopard ; 2: Royal Bengal Tiger ; 3: Asiatic Lion ; 4: Elephant
explanation: Gir = Asiatic Lion; Kaziranga = One-horned Rhino; Dachigam = Hangul; Keibul Lamjao = Sangai.

subject: Social Science
chapter: Chapter 8: India — Climate, Vegetation and Wildlife
question: What is the phenomenon of 'Western Disturbances' that brings winter rainfall and mountain snowfall to north-western India in December and January?
options: Temperate cyclonic low-pressure systems originating over the Mediterranean Sea that are carried eastward into India by the subtropical westerly jet stream
Cyclones from the Bay of Bengal
explanation: Mediterranean extra-tropical cyclones steered by westerly jet streams provide crucial rabi crop (wheat) moisture in northwest India.

subject: Social Science
chapter: Chapter 8: India — Climate, Vegetation and Wildlife
question: Why is the Tibetan Antelope ('Chiru') illegally hunted and endangered in high-altitude Himalayas?
options: For its ultra-fine, warm, and lightweight wool called 'Shahtoosh', which is spun into expensive luxury shawls
explanation: Chiru is poached for Shahtoosh ('King of Wools'), prompting strict international CITES Appendix I trade bans.

subject: Social Science
chapter: Chapter 8: India — Climate, Vegetation and Wildlife
question: What ecological role do coastal Mangrove forests perform during violent tropical cyclones and tsunamis?
options: Their dense root networks absorb and attenuate high-energy oceanic storm surges, drastically reducing inland coastal erosion and protecting human lives
explanation: Mangrove bioshields act as natural coastal wave attenuators, dampening destructive hydro-dynamic surge energies.

subject: Social Science
chapter: Chapter 8: India — Climate, Vegetation and Wildlife
question: What is the primary conservation objective of establishing 'Wildlife Corridors' between fragmented National Parks and Tiger Reserves?
options: To enable safe, unobstructed seasonal migration, gene flow, and territorial dispersal of wildlife populations, preventing inbreeding depression
To build tourist highways through forests
To separate male and female animals
explanation: Landscape ecological corridors connect fragmented habitats, preventing genetic bottlenecks and human-wildlife conflict.

subject: Social Science
chapter: Chapter 8: India — Climate, Vegetation and Wildlife
question: What fundamental message does the final chapter of NCERT Class 6 Geography emphasize regarding wildlife coexistence?
options: Refusing to purchase items made from animal parts (bones, horns, fur, feathers, ivory), planting native trees, and respecting all biological life on Earth
Cutting down all forests for cities
Keeping wild tigers as domestic pets
explanation: NCERT urges ethical consumer boycotts of wildlife derivatives and active community afforestation for ecological sustainability.

subject: Hindi Grammar
question: संज्ञा के स्थान पर प्रयुक्त होने वाले शब्दों (जैसे: मैं, तुम, वह, हम, आप, यह, कोई, क्या) को व्याकरण में क्या कहते हैं?
explanation: संज्ञा की पुनरुक्ति को रोककर वाक्य को सुंदर व संक्षिप्त बनाने वाले विकारी शब्द 'सर्वनाम' कहलाते हैं।

subject: Hindi Grammar
question: हिंदी भाषा में सर्वनाम के मुख्य रूप से कितने भेद (प्रकार) होते हैं?
explanation: सर्वनाम के 6 प्रमुख भेद हैं: 1. पुरुषवाचक, 2. निश्चयवाचक, 3. अनिश्चयवाचक, 4. संबंधवाचक, 5. प्रश्नवाचक, और 6. निजवाचक।

subject: Hindi Grammar
question: बोलने वाले (वक्ता), सुनने वाले (श्रोता) अथवा किसी अन्य व्यक्ति के लिए प्रयुक्त होने वाले सर्वनाम को क्या कहते हैं?
explanation: संवाद में तीनों पुरुषों (वक्ता, श्रोता, अन्य) के लिए प्रयुक्त सर्वनाम 'पुरुषवाचक सर्वनाम' कहलाता है।

subject: Hindi Grammar
question: पुरुषवाचक सर्वनाम के कितने भेद होते हैं?
options: तीन भेद (उत्तम पुरुष, मध्यम पुरुष, और अन्य पुरुष)
explanation: पुरुषवाचक के 3 भेद हैं: उत्तम पुरुष (First Person - मैं/हम), मध्यम पुरुष (Second Person - तू/तुम/आप), अन्य पुरुष (Third Person - वह/वे)।

subject: Hindi Grammar
question: बोलने वाला (वक्ता) या लिखने वाला अपने लिए जिन सर्वनाम शब्दों का प्रयोग करता है (जैसे: मैं, हम, मुझे, मेरा, हमारा), वे क्या कहलाते हैं?
explanation: वक्ता द्वारा स्वयं के संदर्भ में प्रयुक्त पद 'उत्तम पुरुष' कहलाते हैं।

subject: Hindi Grammar
question: जिससे बात की जाए (श्रोता/सुनने वाले) के लिए जिन सर्वनाम शब्दों का प्रयोग होता है (जैसे: तू, तुम, आप, तुझे, तुम्हारा, आपका), वे क्या कहलाते हैं?
explanation: श्रोता के लिए प्रयुक्त सर्वनाम पद 'मध्यम पुरुष' कहलाते हैं।

subject: Hindi Grammar
question: वक्ता और श्रोता जिसके विषय में बात कर रहे हों (किसी तीसरे व्यक्ति) के लिए प्रयुक्त सर्वनाम (जैसे: वह, वे, उसे, उनका, उन्होंने) क्या कहलाते हैं?
explanation: अनुपस्थित या किसी अन्य व्यक्ति के लिए प्रयुक्त पद 'अन्य पुरुष' कहलाते हैं।

subject: Hindi Grammar
question: जो सर्वनाम शब्द किसी निश्चित व्यक्ति, वस्तु या स्थान का निश्चित संकेत करते हैं (जैसे: 'यह मेरी पुस्तक है', 'वह रोहन का घर है'), उन्हें क्या कहते हैं?
options: निश्चयवाचक सर्वनाम या संकेतवाचक सर्वनाम (Demonstrative Pronoun)
explanation: निश्चित दूरस्थ या निकटवर्ती वस्तु की ओर संकेत करने वाले सर्वनाम (यह, वह, ये, वे) 'निश्चयवाचक' कहलाते हैं।

subject: Hindi Grammar
question: जिन सर्वनाम शब्दों से किसी निश्चित व्यक्ति या वस्तु का बोध नहीं होता (जैसे: 'दूध में कुछ गिर गया है', 'दरवाजे पर कोई खड़ा है'), उन्हें क्या कहते हैं?
explanation: अस्पष्ट या अनिर्दिष्ट संज्ञा के स्थान पर आने वाले शब्द (कोई, कुछ, किसी) 'अनिश्चयवाचक सर्वनाम' कहलाते हैं।

subject: Hindi Grammar
question: वाक्य में एक संज्ञा या सर्वनाम का दूसरे संज्ञा या सर्वनाम से संबंध जोड़ने वाले शब्द (जैसे: 'जो मेहनत करेगा, वह सफल होगा', 'जिसकी लाठी उसकी भैंस') क्या कहलाते हैं?
explanation: पारस्परिक उपवाक्यों में संबंध प्रकट करने वाले सर्वनाम युग्म 'संबंधवाचक' कहलाते हैं।

subject: Hindi Grammar
question: जिन सर्वनाम शब्दों का प्रयोग किसी व्यक्ति, वस्तु या घटना के विषय में प्रश्न पूछने के लिए किया जाता है (जैसे: 'तुम्हारा नाम क्या है?', 'वहाँ कौन आया है?'), उन्हें क्या कहते हैं?
explanation: जिज्ञासा व प्रश्न पूछने हेतु प्रयुक्त सर्वनाम (कौन, क्या, किसे, किसका) 'प्रश्नवाचक सर्वनाम' कहलाते हैं।

subject: Hindi Grammar
question: जिन सर्वनाम शब्दों का प्रयोग कर्ता स्वयं अपने लिए (अपने आप के अर्थ में) करता है (जैसे: 'मैं अपना काम स्वयं करूँगा', 'वह खुद चला गया', 'आप ही कर लो'), उन्हें क्या कहते हैं?
explanation: कर्ता द्वारा आत्मबोध (स्वयं/खुद/अपने आप) हेतु प्रयुक्त सर्वनाम 'निजवाचक सर्वनाम' कहलाता है।

subject: Hindi Grammar
question:
वाक्य में प्रयुक्त रेखांकित शब्द का सही सर्वनाम भेद पहचानिए:
'दाल में **कुछ** काला है।'
यहाँ 'कुछ' कौन-सा सर्वनाम है?
options: अनिश्चयवाचक सर्वनाम (वस्तु के लिए अनिश्चितता का बोध)
explanation: 'कुछ' अप्राणीवाचक अनिश्चयवाचक सर्वनाम है, जो किसी अज्ञात वस्तु का संकेत करता है।

subject: Hindi Grammar
question:
वाक्य में प्रयुक्त रेखांकित शब्द का सही सर्वनाम भेद पहचानिए:
'दरवाजे पर **कोई** घंटी बजा रहा है।'
यहाँ 'कोई' कौन-सा सर्वनाम है?
options: अनिश्चयवाचक सर्वनाम (प्राणी/व्यक्ति के लिए अनिश्चितता का बोध)
explanation: 'कोई' प्राणीवाचक अनिश्चयवाचक सर्वनाम है।

subject: Hindi Grammar
question: 'आप' शब्द का प्रयोग मध्यम पुरुष और निजवाचक दोनों में होता है। निम्नलिखित में से किस वाक्य में 'आप' का प्रयोग 'निजवाचक सर्वनाम' के रूप में हुआ है?
options: 'मैं यह काम आप (स्वयं) ही कर लूँगा।' (निजवाचक)
'आप कहाँ जा रहे हैं?' (आदरार्थक मध्यम पुरुष)
explanation: जब 'आप' का अर्थ 'स्वयं/खुद' (अपने आप) हो तो वह निजवाचक सर्वनाम होता है; जब आदरपूर्वक श्रोता के लिए हो तो मध्यम पुरुष होता है।

subject: Hindi Grammar
question: सर्वनाम और सार्वनामिक विशेषण में क्या मूलभूत अंतर होता है?
options: जब 'यह/वह' संज्ञा के स्थान पर अकेले आते हैं तो सर्वनाम होते हैं (जैसे: 'यह मेरी कार है') ; किन्तु जब वे संज्ञा शब्द के ठीक पहले आकर उसकी विशेषता बताते हैं तो सार्वनामिक विशेषण कहलाते हैं (जैसे: 'यह कार मेरी है')
सार्वनामिक विशेषण में संज्ञा नहीं होती
दोनों में कोई अंतर नहीं है
explanation: संज्ञा के स्थान पर प्रयुक्त अकेला पद = सर्वनाम; संज्ञा के आगे लगकर निर्देश करने वाला पद = सार्वनामिक विशेषण।

subject: Hindi Grammar
question:
वाक्य में प्रयुक्त रेखांकित पदों का सही सर्वनाम भेद बताइए:
'**जो** बोएगा, **सो** काटेगा।'
explanation: 'जो' और 'सो' दो परस्पर आश्रित उपवाक्यों को जोड़ने वाले संबंधवाचक सर्वनाम हैं।

subject: Hindi Grammar
question:
वाक्य में प्रयुक्त रेखांकित पद का सर्वनाम भेद बताइए:
'यह चित्र मैंने **खुद** बनाया है।'
options: निजवाचक सर्वनाम ('खुद' कर्ता के स्वयं के संदर्भ में)
explanation: 'खुद' शब्द कर्ता के आत्म-व्यापार का बोध कराता है, अतः निजवाचक सर्वनाम है।

subject: Hindi Grammar
question:
वाक्य में प्रयुक्त रेखांकित पद का सर्वनाम भेद बताइए:
'**वह** बहुत सुंदर गाती है।'
explanation: 'वह' तीसरे व्यक्ति (अनुपस्थित कर्ता) का बोध कराता है, अतः अन्य पुरुषवाचक सर्वनाम है।

subject: Hindi Grammar
question:
वाक्य में प्रयुक्त रेखांकित पद का सर्वनाम भेद बताइए:
'**यह** मेरा विद्यालय है।'
options: निश्चयवाचक सर्वनाम (निकटवर्ती निश्चित वस्तु/स्थान का संकेत)
explanation: 'यह' निकटवर्ती निश्चित संज्ञा की ओर इंगित करने वाला निश्चयवाचक सर्वनाम है।

subject: Hindi Grammar
question: सर्वनाम शब्दों में लिंग का निर्धारण किस आधार पर होता है?
options: सर्वनाम का रूप दोनों लिंगों में समान रहता है; लिंग की पहचान वाक्य में प्रयुक्त क्रिया पद से होती है (जैसे: 'वह पढ़ता है' - पुल्लिंग ; 'वह पढ़ती है' - स्त्रीलिंग)
explanation: सर्वनाम स्वयं लिंग-निरपेक्ष होते हैं (वह, मैं, तुम); उनका लिंग वाक्य की समापिका क्रिया से स्पष्ट होता है।

subject: Hindi Grammar
question:
वाक्य को सर्वनाम की दृष्टि से शुद्ध कीजिए:
'मेरे को आपकी कलम चाहिए।'
options: मुझे आपकी कलम चाहिए। ('मेरे को' के स्थान पर 'मुझे' मानक शुद्ध रूप है)
explanation: हिंदी मानक व्याकरण में 'मेरे को/तेरे को' अमानक बोलचाल है; मानक लिखित रूप 'मुझे/तुझे' है।

subject: Hindi Grammar
question:
वाक्य को शुद्ध कीजिए:
'वह लोग कल दिल्ली जा रहे हैं।'
options: वे लोग कल दिल्ली जा रहे हैं। (बहुवचन संज्ञा 'लोग' के साथ बहुवचन सर्वनाम 'वे' शुद्ध है)
उसे लोग दिल्ली जा रहे हैं।
उन लोग दिल्ली जा रहा है।
explanation: बहुवचन कर्ता के साथ अन्य पुरुष का बहुवचन रूप 'वे' प्रयुक्त होना चाहिए।

subject: Hindi Grammar
question: सर्वनाम शब्द 'जो' के विभिन्न कारक रूपों का सही युग्म कौन-सा है?
explanation: संबंधवाचक सर्वनाम 'जो' के कारक रूप 'जिस-' प्रातिपदिक से बनते हैं (जिसने, जिसे, जिससे, जिसका)।

subject: Hindi Grammar
question: प्रश्नवाचक सर्वनाम 'कौन' और 'क्या' का प्रयोग क्रमशः किनके लिए होता है?
options: 'कौन' का प्रयोग सजीव प्राणियों (व्यक्तियों) के लिए तथा 'क्या' का प्रयोग निर्जीव वस्तुओं या घटनाओं के लिए होता है
'क्या' केवल इंसानों के लिए आता है
दोनों केवल जानवरों के लिए आते हैं
explanation: प्राणीवाचक प्रश्न = 'कौन' (बाहर कौन है?); अप्राणीवाचक प्रश्न = 'क्या' (हाथ में क्या है?)।

subject: Hindi Grammar
question:
वाक्य में प्रयुक्त रेखांकित पद का सर्वनाम भेद बताइए:
'गांधी जी महान राष्ट्रपिता थे। **आपने** देश को आज़ाद कराया।'
options: अन्य पुरुषवाचक सर्वनाम (आदरार्थक रूप में किसी तीसरे ऐतिहासिक महापुरुष के परिचय में 'आप' का प्रयोग)
explanation: किसी प्रतिष्ठित अन्य व्यक्ति (Third Person) के जीवन परिचय या उल्लेख में आदर प्रकट करने हेतु 'आप' अन्य पुरुष के रूप में प्रयुक्त होता है।

subject: Hindi Grammar
question: सर्वनाम के साथ जब दो कारक चिह्न (विभक्तियाँ) एक साथ आती हैं, तो उन्हें कैसे लिखा जाता है?
options: पहला कारक चिह्न सर्वनाम से मिलाकर और दूसरा अलग लिखा जाता है (जैसे: 'उसके लिए', 'उनमें से')
दोनों अलग लिखे जाते हैं ('उस के लिए')
explanation: मानक हिंदी वर्तनी नियम: 'उसके लिए' में पहला परसर्ग 'के' संश्लिष्ट तथा दूसरा 'लिए' विश्लिष्ट लिखा जाता है।

subject: Hindi Grammar
question:
वाक्य में प्रयुक्त रेखांकित पद का सर्वनाम भेद बताइए:
'**जिसकी** लाठी **उसकी** भैंस।'
explanation: 'जिसकी-उसकी' लोकोक्ति में दो संज्ञाओं के अधिकार संबंध को जोड़ने वाले संबंधवाचक सर्वनाम हैं।

subject: Hindi Grammar
question:
कथन और कारण को ध्यानपूर्वक पढ़ें:
कथन (A): 'यह घड़ी मेरी है' में 'यह' सार्वनामिक विशेषण है, जबकि 'यह मेरी घड़ी है' में 'यह' निश्चयवाचक सर्वनाम है।
कारण (R): सार्वनामिक विशेषण में सर्वनाम पद संज्ञा शब्द ('घड़ी') के तुरंत पहले आकर उसकी ओर संकेत करता है, जबकि सर्वनाम संज्ञा के स्थान पर स्वतंत्र प्रयुक्त होता है।
सही विकल्प चुनें:
options: (A) और (R) दोनों सही हैं तथा (R), (A) की सही व्याख्या करता है।
(A) और (R) दोनों सही हैं, परन्तु (R), (A) की सही व्याख्या नहीं करता।
explanation: संज्ञा से पूर्व प्रयुक्त सर्वनाम विशेषण बन जाता है (यह घड़ी), जबकि स्वतंत्र प्रयुक्त पद निश्चयवाचक सर्वनाम होता है (यह मेरी घड़ी है)।

subject: Hindi Grammar
question:
Spot the IMPOSTER in the following group of सर्वनाम और उनके भेदों के युग्म में:
Group: [हम - उत्तम पुरुष, तुम - मध्यम पुरुष, कोई - अनिश्चयवाचक, स्वयं - प्रश्नवाचक]
explanation: 'स्वयं - प्रश्नवाचक' अशुद्ध युग्म है; 'स्वयं' निजवाचक सर्वनाम (Reflexive Pronoun) होता है, प्रश्नवाचक नहीं।

subject: Hindi Grammar
question:
सुमेलित कीजिए (सर्वनाम शब्द और उनके व्याकरणिक भेद):
(क) हम      -> (i) अनिश्चयवाचक सर्वनाम
(ख) कोई     -> (ii) उत्तम पुरुषवाचक सर्वनाम
(ग) जो-वह   -> (iii) निजवाचक सर्वनाम
(घ) अपने आप -> (iv) संबंधवाचक सर्वनाम
explanation: हम = उत्तम पुरुष; कोई = अनिश्चयवाचक; जो-वह = संबंधवाचक; अपने आप = निजवाचक।

subject: Hindi Grammar
question:
निम्नलिखित वाक्य में प्रयुक्त सर्वनामों की सही संख्या और भेद पहचानिए:
'**मैं** **अपना** काम **स्वयं** करूँगा और **उसे** **कुछ** नहीं दूँगा।'
इस वाक्य में कुल कितने सर्वनाम पद आए हैं?
options: 5 सर्वनाम पद (मैं = उत्तम पुरुष, अपना = निजवाचक, स्वयं = निजवाचक, उसे = अन्य पुरुष, कुछ = अनिश्चयवाचक)
explanation: पाँच सर्वनाम पद: 'मैं' (उत्तम पुरुष), 'अपना' (निजवाचक), 'स्वयं' (निजवाचक), 'उसे' (अन्य पुरुष), 'कुछ' (अनिश्चयवाचक)।

subject: Hindi Grammar
question: सर्वनाम शब्दों में किस कारक की विभक्ति का प्रयोग पूर्णतः वर्जित होता है (अर्थात् वह कारक सर्वनाम में नहीं होता)?
options: संबोधन कारक (हे!, अरे! - सर्वनामों का संबोधन नहीं होता, जैसे 'हे तुम!', 'अरे मैं!' अमानक हैं)
explanation: सर्वनाम में संबोधन कारक नहीं होता; अतः सर्वनाम के 7 कारक रूप ही बनते हैं (संबोधन रहित)।

subject: Hindi Grammar
question: अनिश्चयवाचक सर्वनाम 'कोई' का तिर्यक (सपरसर्ग) बहुवचन रूप क्या होता है?
options: किन्हीं (जैसे: 'किन्हीं लोगों ने कहा', 'किन्हीं को बुलाओ')
explanation: 'कोई' का एकवचन तिर्यक 'किसी' तथा बहुवचन तिर्यक 'किन्हीं' (किन्हीं ने, किन्हीं को) होता है।

subject: Hindi Grammar
question: सर्वनाम शब्द 'क्या' का प्रयोग जब विस्मय (आश्चर्य) प्रकट करने के लिए होता है (जैसे: 'क्या शानदार दृश्य है!'), तो वह क्या कहलाता है?
explanation: यहाँ प्रश्न न पूछकर विस्मय/प्रशंसा की जा रही है, अतः यह विस्मयादिबोधक अव्यय के रूप में प्रयुक्त हुआ है।

subject: Hindi Grammar
question:
वाक्य में प्रयुक्त रेखांकित पदों के सर्वनाम भेदों का सही क्रम बताइए:
'**आप** बैठिए, **मैं** **स्वयं** देख लूँगा कि **कौन** आया है।'
options: आप = मध्यम पुरुष ; मैं = उत्तम पुरुष ; स्वयं = निजवाचक ; कौन = प्रश्नवाचक
आप = निजवाचक ; मैं = अन्य पुरुष ; स्वयं = मध्यम पुरुष ; कौन = अनिश्चयवाचक
explanation: आप (आदरार्थक मध्यम पुरुष), मैं (उत्तम पुरुष), स्वयं (निजवाचक), कौन (प्रश्नवाचक)।

subject: Hindi Grammar
question:
वाक्य को मानक हिंदी व्याकरण के अनुसार शुद्ध कीजिए:
'तेरे को क्या चाहिए?'
explanation: 'तेरे को' अमानक रूप है; मध्यम पुरुष कर्म कारक में 'तुझे' या 'आपको' शुद्ध है।

subject: Hindi Grammar
question: संयुक्त सर्वनाम (Compound Pronoun) का सही उदाहरण कौन-सा है?
options: जो कोई, कोई न कोई, कुछ न कुछ, सब कुछ, और कोई
explanation: डॉ. दीमशित्स के अनुसार दो सर्वनामों के संयोग से बनने वाले पद 'संयुक्त सर्वनाम' कहलाते हैं (जो कोई, कोई न कोई, सब कुछ)।

subject: Hindi Grammar
question:
वाक्य में प्रयुक्त रेखांकित पद का सही सर्वनाम भेद बताइए:
'घर में **सब कुछ** लुट गया।'
explanation: 'सब कुछ' संयुक्त अनिश्चयवाचक सर्वनाम है, जो समस्त वस्तुओं का अनिश्चित संकलन प्रस्तुत करता है।

subject: Hindi Grammar
question: सर्वनाम की उपयोगिता के संदर्भ में कौन-सा कथन सर्वाधिक सटीक है?
options: सर्वनाम भाषा को सहज, संक्षिप्त, प्रवाहपूर्ण और पुनरुक्ति दोष से मुक्त बनाते हैं, जिससे भाषा की अभिव्यक्ति क्षमता उत्कृष्ट हो जाती है
सर्वनाम केवल संस्कृत में उपयोगी हैं
सर्वनाम से वाक्य कठिन हो जाते हैं
सर्वनाम का कोई व्याकरणिक महत्व नहीं है
explanation: संज्ञा की बार-बार होने वाली अप्रिय पुनरावृत्ति से मुक्ति दिलाकर भाषा में प्रवाह और लालित्य उत्पन्न करना सर्वनाम का मुख्य प्रयोजन है।
